prompt:
Design and implement the architecture that brings the separately managed VMware estate in `testdata/estate.json` under one VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 fleet. This is an architecture deliverable, not an explanatory report.

Before implementing it, use genuine network research against currently reachable Broadcom-published compatibility, interoperability, release-note, and upgrade-path sources. Consult enough primary material to confirm the supported combinations and sequencing for every product in the inventory, including Live Site Recovery. Record each source you actually consulted in `research.md` with its title, URL, access date, and the architecture decision it informed. The local compatibility snapshot is the deterministic implementation authority, not a substitute for this live research; no particular query or URL is prescribed.

Implement package `vcfarch` in Go. Complete `BuildArchitecture(Inventory, CompatibilitySnapshot) (Architecture, error)` and add table-driven unit tests. Commit the generated machine-readable result as `architecture.json`. The result must contain: (1) `greenfieldSddcSpec`, a greenfield `SddcSpec` valid against `components.schemas.SddcSpec` in `specifications/vcf-installer/vcf-installer-openapi.json`, vendored from tag `9.1.0.0` of the Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository; (2) `topology`, placing one stretched management domain across exactly the two data sites and placing its vSAN witness at the inventory's independent third failure domain, outside both data sites and outside the management-domain host set; and (3) `migrationPlan`, an ordered plan conforming to `migration-plan.schema.json`.

The migration plan must contain exactly one step for every inventory component. Each step must preserve the component ID, type, site, and current version; name its target product and version; choose an allowed action; and name every gate required by `testdata/compatibility-snapshot.json`. Its order must satisfy every dependency expressed by those gates. Use the pinned snapshot as the authoritative compatibility contract if live Broadcom content has changed. Treat the supplied inventory, snapshot, schemas, installer specification, license, and contract tests as read-only. Keep `BuildArchitecture` deterministic and ensure the committed `architecture.json` is semantically identical to its result for the supplied fixtures. Finish with `go test -race ./...` passing.
verify_cmd: printf '%s\n' 'e3c881cba3bcabea275911eea4058e712980df2b55fa9c4cb3d5e6016a4c882e  schema_test.go' 'a70fb2b6106a0342a67ab414e587007c65538e57184dda227e6886b20c488d50  verifier_test.go' | sha256sum -c - && go test -race -count=1 -timeout 60s ./...
